record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: For any infinitely renormalizable mildly dissipative map in the zero-entropy locus E0, does the sequence of renormalizations converge?

evidence.quote: Question 8. — Let us consider any infinitely renormalizable mildly dissipative map in E0. Does the sequence of renormalizations converge?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $f:D\to D$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism of the closed two-dimensional disk onto its image (with $f(D)\subset \operatorname{int}(D)$). Call $f$ mildly dissipative if for every ergodic $f$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ that is not supported on a hyperbolic sink, and for $\mu$-almost every point $x$, the connected component of the intersection of the Pesin stable manifold $W^s(x)$ with $D$ containing $x$ is unbounded in $W^s(x)$ (equivalently, accumulates on the boundary of $D$ inside $W^s(x)$). Denote by $\mathcal E_0$ the set of mildly dissipative $C^2$ diffeomorphisms $f:D\to D$ with zero topological entropy, $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)=0$.

A map $f\in\mathcal E_0$ is said to be renormalizable if there exists an integer $p\ge 2$ and a topological disk $B\subset D$ such that the iterates $B,f(B),\dots,f^{p-1}(B)$ have pairwise disjoint interiors and $f^p(B)\subset B$; the first-return map $f^p|_B$, rescaled by an affine (or smooth) change of coordinates that normalizes $B$ to a standard disk, is called a renormalization of $f$. The map $f$ is infinitely renormalizable if this procedure can be iterated indefinitely, producing a sequence of renormalizations $R^n f$, $n\ge 1$, each viewed as a diffeomorphism of the standard disk after rescaling.

Question. For every infinitely renormalizable map $f\in\mathcal E_0$, does the sequence $\{R^n f\}_{n\ge 1}$ converge (in the $C^0$, or appropriate $C^r$, topology on maps of the standard disk) as $n\to\infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in the recent open-problems compilation on Hénon maps and is consistent with active research: convergence of renormalizations is established for strongly (highly) dissipative Hénon-like maps via the one-dimensional renormalization fixed point, but for general mildly dissipative maps in the zero-entropy locus, convergence of the renormalization sequence remains an open question, as indicated by ongoing work and seminars on mildly dissipative maps with zero entropy.

status_evidence.snippet: Mildly dissipative zero-entropy disk diffeomorphisms are (generalized) Morse–Smale or infinitely renormalizable.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework E0 in which the question is posed; convergence not asserted in full generality.
